tagline: Two rivers and a very large local legend.
intro: Out of Happy Camp, Highway 96 runs down the Klamath River to Orleans and on to Weitchpec, where the Trinity joins the Klamath. There the highway changes rivers. It follows the Trinity through Hoopa toward Willow Creek, threading communities whose histories reach well beyond the gold camps.

The Karuk Tribe has its headquarters in Happy Camp, and Weitchpec is an ancestral Yurok village. The byway’s more elusive namesake gets a solid introduction at Happy Camp: an eighteen-foot Bigfoot made of recycled metal.

moments.title: Happy Camp
moments.text: Happy Camp gives its local legend eighteen feet of recycled metal, a Bigfoot statue in a town named by gold miners.

moments.title: Orleans
moments.text: Orleans stands on Panamnik, the original Karuk settlement, and in 1855 became the county seat of Klamath County, a county that no longer exists.

moments.title: Weitchpec
moments.text: The Trinity meets the Klamath at Weitchpec, an ancestral Yurok village where Highway 96 turns to follow the other river.

sources.label: USDA Forest Service, Klamath National Forest scenic drives
